newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen moving narrowly.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen moving narrowly.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to move narrowly on Monday after the Nikkei average fell by more than two percent on Friday.
The Nikkei fell on arbitrage-linked selling after a breakdown in the bourse's electronic trading system.
Brokers said bargain-hunting was likely to appear, but there were still few reasons for investors to chase stocks higher and gains would be limited.
On Friday, the Nikkei suffered its sixth-largest point drop this year, ending down 527.05 points, or 2.59 percent, at 19,804.38. Its September futures ended 530 lower at 19,800.
"Pension and public funds could do some fishing at the bottom, but we would be lucky if the Nikkei average were to end above 20,000," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities' general manager, said.
Brokers noted that blue chips, expecially high technology issues, had not fallen in tandem with the indices and the market was watching when that situation would change.
"Blue chips are holding up the market at the moment and once shares like Sony Corp start slowing down, the atmosphere could change," one broker said.
Market sources expect a range of 19,550 to 20,050.
